slides.title: Non-repudiation
slides.teach: Non-repudiation provides proof that someone performed an action so they cannot reasonably deny doing it later.

course.learn: Non-repudiation provides proof that someone performed an action so they cannot reasonably deny doing it later.

breakdown.explanation: You cannot say you did not do it when reliable evidence ties the action to you.
Digital signatures, audit logs, timestamps, and signed transactions.

course.why: Organizations may need strong evidence showing who approved, signed, sent, or performed an important action.
course.example: A manager digitally signs a transaction and later claims they never approved it.
course.exam: Look for prove, cannot deny, signed, evidence, or proof of approval.
course.check_q: A company needs proof that a manager approved a transaction and cannot later deny it. Which concept applies?

hero.title: Non-repudiation
hero.intro: Understand how security systems provide evidence that an action was performed so it cannot reasonably be denied later.

blocks.title: Can't deny it
blocks.prompt: Can the action be proven later?

cards.name: Non-repudiation
cards.definition: Providing proof that someone performed an action so they cannot reasonably deny doing it later.

blocks.title: Can they deny the action later?
items: Non-repudiation provides evidence tying an action to a person or system so they cannot reasonably deny performing it later.
Example: A manager digitally signs a transaction and later claims they never approved it.
blocks.example: Common clues: digital signatures, signed transactions, timestamps, and audit evidence.

questions.q: A company needs proof that a manager approved a transaction and cannot later deny it. Which concept applies?
questions.explanation: Non-repudiation provides evidence tying an action to the person who performed it.

questions.q: Which technology BEST supports proof that a particular party signed a document?
questions.explanation: A digital signature can provide cryptographic evidence associated with the signer and the signed data.

questions.q: A user later claims they never approved a change, but signed logs and timestamps show the approval. Which concept is being supported?
questions.explanation: The evidence makes it difficult for the user to reasonably deny the action.

questions.q: Which phrase is the strongest clue for non-repudiation in a Security+ scenario?
questions.explanation: Non-repudiation focuses on evidence that prevents reasonable denial of an action.
